_comment: Population anchors for the Hong Kong avifauna timeline. NOTHING HERE IS SMOOTHED: anchors are the source of truth and everything between them is derived at build time. Species with no recording in calls/ are skipped by compose.py and wait here until one arrives.

_basis._comment: How much weight each anchor carries. Only 'documented' is treated as established fact; the viewer draws every other kind as a dashed stretch of rim.
_basis.documented: The cited source was opened and the figure read back off it, or derived by stated arithmetic from a figure that was.
_basis.secondary: Taken from a compiled series that agrees with the verified figures around it, but whose individual year has not been checked against the primary report. Plausible and probably right - not yet proof.
_basis.estimated: A bound, a range, a period midpoint, or a placeholder. NOT a measurement, and must never be cited as one.

_sources.avifauna: Carey, G. J., M. R. Leven and C. C. Pang (2023), The Avifauna of Hong Kong, HKBWS - https://avifauna.hkbws.org.hk
_sources._note: Deep Bay waterbird counts after 1998 come from the AFCD/HKBWS Mai Po Inner Deep Bay Ramsar Site Waterbird Monitoring Programme. Summary figures published in the sources above are quoted with attribution; the raw programme data is HKSAR Government copyright and would need written AFCD permission to reuse.

_metrics._comment: Abundance in Hong Kong is not recorded the same way for every bird, and pretending otherwise is the easiest way to lie with this piece. Waterbirds are counted in Deep Bay; passerines are not, and are known from passage counts; widespread residents are known only from atlas occupancy. Each species declares its metric and the viewer scales and labels within it, never across.

This is an autumn passage series - the highest single count recorded in each cited year, at varying sites - not a census of birds present. species._data_status: The densest series in this project: a near-annual run from the first International Synchronous Census in 1994 to 2026. THE POINT OF THIS SPECIES: globally it is a conservation success - 7,746 birds in 2026, a record - while Deep Bay peaked at 462 in 2010 and has hovered near 300-380 ever since. Its share of the world population fell from over a fifth in 2011 to 4.4% in 2026. It is the voice that survives to the end and still represents a loss. NOTE ON 411: an earlier anchor placed 411 in 2016 from the 2026 report's phrase 'the peak of 411 recorded ten years ago'. The compiled series puts 411 in 2011 and again in 2015, and 371 in 2016; the 2011 reading is corroborated independently, since the 2024 report states Deep Bay held 'over 20%' of the world population in 2011 and 411/1848 is 22.2%. The 2016=411 reading is withdrawn. ACOUSTIC CAVEAT: near-silent on the wintering grounds.
